_note: §1a.6: no module ships without a learning / reasoning / depth verdict, each
pass or fail with the evidence named. `n/a` is a first-class answer - a
Parquet writer does not reason - but it must be stated, not left blank.
A verdict is a judgement and this file is where the judgement is recorded.
What is CHECKED mechanically by `integrity.axis_verdicts` is that every axis
is answered, that the answer is one of pass/fail/n/a, and that every named
artifact is on disk. A verdict citing a test nobody wrote fails the check.
Completed 2026-08-09 for every module in src/. Four carry an explicit FAIL
and that is the point of the exercise: a standard that produces only passes
is a standard nobody fails. Three fail DEPTH because nothing calls them - a
module that cannot run cannot change what the system does when it is wrong,
which is the master test - and one because no test exercises it at all.

validation.breadth.learning: pass: no constant in the decision path is typed. The trigger threshold is a percentile of each symbol's OWN history (L1), and the collapse band 5-15 is quoted from §5a.4 rather than chosen here - a gate that picked its own threshold would be grading itself against a number selected to pass
validation.breadth.reasoning: pass: it distinguishes clustered arrivals from correlated outcomes and says which it found. The first draft read §5a.4's 'cluster AND correlate' as a disjunction and would have reported REDESIGN on data the spec does not call one; the conjunction is now pinned by a test
validation.breadth.depth: pass: changes behaviour when wrong. REDESIGN is a reachable verdict that stops Phase 4, and INCONCLUSIVE is returned rather than a number whenever the sample cannot support one

validation.promotion_pipeline.learning: pass: every configuration scored is a Trial Registry entry, and the N that deflates the winner is the registry's cumulative count (L7) - a wider search raises its own bar
validation.promotion_pipeline.reasoning: pass: it caught a lookahead in its own candidate. Pure noise scored Sharpe 3.90 and passed three of five gates; the return definition was selecting on information that had not settled. Both the noise case and the real-edge case are tests, because a stack that refuses everything measures nothing
validation.promotion_pipeline.depth: pass: the master test. A refusal is the designed outcome, and the gates compose with AND so no single one can be outvoted

risk.tail_cap.depth: pass: a missing ceiling FAILS rather than being skipped, and paper breaches are recorded as `would_have_breached` instead of being silently unenforced

capture.capture_console.learning: n/a: a display. Nothing is fitted

capture.capture_console.depth: pass: cleared 2026-08-09, having failed for having no test at all. It also needs no server process that could itself die and take the view with it

capture.venues.deribit.learning: n/a: a capture adapter. Nothing is fitted
capture.venues.deribit.reasoning: pass: it is polled rather than subscribed because one request returns the whole chain against 1,502 websocket channels, and it declines to capture DVOL because that series IS backfillable while the chain is not - the endpoint ignores a `timestamp` parameter and returns the current chain, which is the entire argument for capturing today rather than when a feature needs it
capture.venues.deribit.depth: pass: nulls are carried through untouched because they are real market structure - `bid_price` is null on 89 of 818 BTC instruments and `high`/`low` on 588, and the prior-art client in nse-crypto-bot-final coerced exactly those fields with `float(x or 0.0)`, inventing a bid of zero that makes a worthless option look free. A JSON-RPC error body is refused before it can be split under every instrument in the last good chain, and the two currencies polled were measured against the live venue - 49 of Deribit's 51 currencies list no options at all. Verified by running it: 1,502 files, 3,822 records, 0 dropped and 0 malformed, and 401 null bids still null after a round trip through the archive

store.option_chain.learning: n/a: a projection of archived polls. Nothing is fitted
store.option_chain.reasoning: pass: it distinguishes an ABSENT value from a zero one, which is the whole difficulty of an option chain - `bid_price` is null on 89 of 818 BTC instruments because nobody will buy that strike at any price, while `mark_price` is genuinely 0.0 on others because a deep out-of-the-money strike days from expiry marks at nothing. The prior-art client collapsed both with `float(x or 0.0)`. It also declines to compute greeks: the venue publishes none, and a delta computed in a feature module is one whose model and rate assumptions are ours and testable, where a venue field is neither
store.option_chain.depth: pass: it is reachable - registered in `build_polled.DATASETS` and built by `store_supervisor.sh` the same day the capture landed, because a captured tape no builder reads is this codebase's named failure and has happened twice. Units are in the column name (`mark_iv_fraction`, converted once from the venue's percent) since a column called `mark_iv` holding 41.42 beside a model expecting 0.4142 is wrong by 100x in a way no presence check catches, and `quote_currency` is carried because a BTC option marks in COINS not dollars. Verified against the real archive: 19,130 records, 19,130 quotes, 0 refused, all 1,502 instrument names parsed, and absence stayed separable from zero at 1,957 null bids against 373 real zero marks

store.live_bars.learning: n/a: a build entry point. Nothing is fitted
store.live_bars.reasoning: pass: it publishes provisional bars WITHOUT re-stamping availability, so the complete hourly build - whose stamp is derived from the data and is therefore EARLIER than any wall clock - still supersedes them under `drop_duplicates(keep="last")`. The first version stamped `now` and would have made every provisional bar permanent in a store with no delete path
store.live_bars.depth: pass: the minute containing the newest readable trade is dropped rather than published, because the readable prefix ends inside the last flush interval and that minute is missing trades that already happened. A file with nothing flushed yet is counted apart from a symbol with no trades - the exact pair `store.cli` skips the whole live hour to avoid confusing. Measured against the real archive: lag from 69 minutes to 30-90 seconds, and a second pass over the same hour writes 0 bars rather than a duplicate copy per minute

store.cli.reasoning: pass: it builds from EVENT time with a bounded lookahead rather than from the folder a frame landed in, and drops only what is known not to be dollar-quoted - unknown and unlisted are built and named
store.cli.depth: pass: a trade no build will ever read is quarantined and counted rather than dropped, and a live hour is skipped rather than read as an empty market

store.funding_rates.depth: pass: no observations is an empty frame, never a zero rate - charging zero funding to a carry strategy is the optimistic default, not the conservative one

store.build_polled.depth: pass: a live hour is skipped rather than read, and no rows appends nothing rather than writing an empty dataset over the old one

store.quote_currency.depth: pass: never parsed from the symbol string, because BTCU is BTC quoted in U and XRPRLUSD is quoted in RLUSD

cost.fee_fetcher.depth: pass: a stale verification is reported as stale - tiers move with 30-day volume, so an old fetch is a historical fact rather than a current one

cost.round_trip_cost.reasoning: pass: it REFUSES rather than defaulting when an input is missing or stale, and the refusal names what was missing - a quote produced from a default is the flattering answer
cost.round_trip_cost.depth: pass: the master test. It changes what happens when the system does not know something, by declining to price the trade

cost.funding_carry.reasoning: pass: the rate used at a settlement is the last one KNOWN at that settlement, never the newest - and a settlement with no prior observation raises rather than borrowing
cost.funding_carry.depth: pass: funding is charged at actual settlement times rather than smoothed, which is the difference between a carry cost and an average

execution.order_intent_wal.reasoning: pass: the intent is durable BEFORE the request is sent, so an unknown outcome is recoverable rather than invisible - and it never blind-retries
execution.order_intent_wal.depth: pass: it changes what happens after a crash, which is the only moment it exists for

execution.order_lifecycle.reasoning: pass: state is remaining quantity rather than a filled flag, because a partial fill is the normal case and a boolean cannot hold it
execution.order_lifecycle.depth: pass: a partially filled order cannot be mistaken for a complete one, which is what stops a double-send

execution.state_recovery.depth: fail: cannot change what the system does, because nothing calls it. It needs venue truth from an authenticated session that does not exist, so the refusal it is built around can never fire. Tracked as RX-005, the last baselined unsupported claim

ops.rate_budget.learning: n/a: a token bucket. Capacities are measured from venue headers and disclosed, which is L1's permitted case
ops.rate_budget.reasoning: pass: the budget is shared through a locked state file rather than held per process, because two processes each within the limit are together over it
ops.rate_budget.depth: pass: it refuses a poll that cannot afford its weight, and a refused poll is cheaper than a per-IP ban that scales to three days

ops.venue_halt.learning: n/a: a state machine over health reports. Nothing is fitted
ops.venue_halt.reasoning: pass: it halts on corruption alone and REFUSES to halt on silence, with the reason written where the limit is set - the silence count is inflated by thin tail symbols and by a feed the venue withholds, so it cannot tell a sick venue from a wide one
ops.venue_halt.depth: pass: a halt persists across restarts, because a halt a restart clears is one an unhealthy venue escapes by killing the watcher; and recovery needs a sustained dwell rather than one clean sample

ops.watchdog.learning: n/a: a kill switch. Nothing is fitted
ops.watchdog.reasoning: pass: it reports honestly which mechanisms fired AND which cannot exist on this host - no sudo, no iptables, no nft, so the firewall half is unavailable and says so rather than reporting success
ops.watchdog.depth: pass: the kill file is written first and unconditionally, so even a half-completed trip stops trading; a later trip does not overwrite the first breach's reason

ops.raw_eviction.learning: n/a: a retention policy. Nothing is fitted
ops.raw_eviction.reasoning: pass: it drops only hours PROVEN to be in the bucket, so the local copy is never the last copy
ops.raw_eviction.depth: pass: retention lives in a file rather than a constant, so changing it does not require redeploying the thing that enforces it

paper.fill_model.learning: n/a: a fill rule with a disclosed participation parameter. Not fitted, and not claimed to be
paper.fill_model.reasoning: pass: it keeps optimistic and pessimistic accountings apart rather than averaging them into one number that is true of neither
paper.fill_model.depth: pass: a resting order that never printed does not fill, so an unfilled signal is visible as unfilled rather than as a trade at a hoped price

paper.market_replay.learning: n/a: it feeds the tape. Nothing is fitted, and a feed that adapted to what it fed would be the leak the clock gate exists to prevent
paper.market_replay.reasoning: pass: replay and forward are the same method called with a different clock rather than two loops that drift apart, and it refuses a reader built without a holdout custodian instead of trusting the caller to have passed one - the holdout's only value is never having been read, and that cannot be checked after the fact. Amended 2026-08-17: reads are now bounded BELOW by an availability watermark, and the choice of availability over event time is the safety argument - a correction to an old bar carries a later availability time by definition, so it still arrives through the bound, while a bound on event time would hide corrections. `mark_seen` marks without constructing a TapeEvent, because `prime` built 2,316,171 of them purely to count them
paper.market_replay.depth: pass: it refuses an unguarded reader at construction, refuses a non-positive price on sight, and counts corrections that arrive after their bar was already traded on instead of re-feeding them. Reachable since scripts/paper_supervisor.sh. The watermark is also what keeps `_emitted` bounded: rows below it are never read again, so the set holds what has ARRIVED rather than everything that exists. `resume_at` documents in its own docstring that the caller must still mark-seen at the bound, because the bound is inclusive and a row sitting exactly on it would otherwise be read with an empty emitted set and TRADED - the 2026-08-15 defect, reachable through the new path if that step were skipped

paper.paper_broker.learning: n/a: a venue model, not a learner. The one estimated quantity it uses - participation - is `paper.participation_calibration`'s to measure, and is carried onto every fill with its calibrated flag rather than absorbed
paper.paper_broker.reasoning: pass: it returns refusals instead of raising them, because `OrderIntentWal` writes outcome=unknown before calling a transport and leaves it there when the transport raises - and unknown is the specific claim that the venue may be holding the order, which for a local refusal is false and would block every later startup reconciliation. It also refuses market and reduce_only orders rather than approximating them
paper.paper_broker.depth: pass: a refusal comes back as a rejection rather than as an exception, so the WAL records a known outcome instead of leaving outcome=unknown on the startup work list forever - the behaviour under error IS the design here. AccountingDiverged raises rather than re-syncing the two books. Reachable since scripts/paper_supervisor.sh

paper.position_book.learning: n/a: it records what was filled. Nothing here is fitted, and a position model that inferred anything would be the wrong kind of clever
paper.position_book.reasoning: pass: it keeps one book per accounting rather than one book holding both, because the average of an optimistic and a pessimistic fill is true of neither, and it omits flat positions because presence in the reconciler's input is a claim that something is held
paper.position_book.depth: pass: it changes what the system does when something is wrong - a flat position is omitted rather than reported at zero, which is what stops recover_and_reconcile refusing every startup after the first closed round trip, and a venue with no declared fee schedule is refused rather than priced at a default. Reachable since scripts/paper_supervisor.sh

paper.participation_calibration.learning: n/a: it would estimate participation from prints, and does not run
paper.participation_calibration.reasoning: pass: the question it asks is the right one - how much of a print a resting order would actually have received, rather than a fixed fraction
paper.participation_calibration.depth: fail: cannot change what the system does, because nothing calls it. `paper.fill_model` still uses a disclosed constant, so the calibration this module exists to supply is not supplied. Clears when the fill model reads it

paper.prove_plumbing.learning: n/a: a crude fixed signal, deliberately - it exists to prove wiring, not edge

features.kyle_lambda.learning: pass: lambda_price_impact is the OLS slope of close-to-close price change on a tick-rule-signed-volume proxy, refit fresh over the newest WINDOW_BARS=120 one-minute bars on every call - not a trained parameter carried forward, a regression run against the window it is reported beside, with the window bounds and observation count riding the row as data rather than staying in the docstring (L1). What would falsify it: on the synthetic zero-noise series built in the tests, a wrong pairing of price change to flow (an off-by-one index, a sign error) would show up as recovery failure, not pass quietly - the fit recovers the constructed coefficient to 1e-9 and R^2 > 0.999999. On a window with a flat close or a flow proxy with no variance it refuses (zero_price_variance / zero_variance_regressor) rather than reporting a fitted number - an ablation that swapped in a fixed placeholder for either check would be caught by those two tests going from a refusal to a spurious pass. The two numbers that are NOT fit - WINDOW_BARS=120 and MIN_OBSERVATIONS=20 - are disclosed design constants in the same register `features.price_divergence` and `features.consolidated_price` already use for their own window and floor
features.kyle_lambda.reasoning: pass: it states its own boundary with a checkable fact rather than a verbal hedge (R4-shaped abstention). Real signed order flow - per-trade buyer/seller side - is not stored anywhere in this build: `capture.venues.binance` does not persist aggTrade's maker flag and `capture.venues.coinbase` does not persist `match.side`, so `store.trade_bars` carries no signed-flow column for this or any other feature to read. Rather than pass `volume` off as signed flow, the regressor is the tick rule (`sign(close_t - close_{t-1}) * volume_t`), named `signed_flow_source` as a column on every row, not only in prose. The docstring and this verdict both say the sharper thing a caller would otherwise have to discover by hand: because the tick rule signs each bar's flow FROM the same price change being regressed on, sign(flow) equals sign(delta_price) by construction whenever the price moved, so the fit can only certify that flow MAGNITUDE tracks move MAGNITUDE, never that flow predicts direction - R^2 here runs higher than a fit against genuine trade-side data would, for a reason that has nothing to do with liquidity. It refuses rather than guesses on three degenerate windows a caller could otherwise be shown a confident number for (too few points, a constant regressor, a constant price step), each pinned by its own test

(3) A venue that settles EVERY hour has no contrast at all: the ratio is 1.0 by construction and a p-value over it is arithmetic on a tautology. features.beta_to_btc.reasoning: pass: it is built around one defect that produces a perfectly normal-looking number. Two symbols' bar series are different lengths - they list at different times, halt at different times, and one of them is thin - so zipping them by position pairs BTC's 09:04 return with an altcoin's 11:17 return and reports a correlation between two unrelated moments. Returns are therefore keyed by the timestamp of the bar that CLOSED them and only shared timestamps contribute, pinned by test_misaligned_series_contribute_only_their_shared_minutes, which offsets one series by an hour in the store and asserts the beta is still exactly 2. beta_and_correlation itself never sees a timestamp, deliberately: an alignment bug should be impossible to introduce there because there is nothing there to align. Overlapping triple-barrier labels violate IID - an event at bar 100 with a 480-bar horizon shares 477 bars with an event at bar 103 - and unweighted training counts that cluster as many independent observations, inflating confidence in proportion to the overlap. Omitting them raises WeightsRequired rather than defaulting to 1.0; a caller may waive them with uniform_weights=True and the waiver is recorded in the trial's own params so a later reader can see whether the correction was applied without re-deriving it from the code of the day. Found by running it: with n_groups=6, k_test=2 there are 15 folds and every group sits in the test set of 5, so concatenating fold predictions produced 3,000 'observations' from 600 rows and the bootstrap computed a p-value on an effective sample five times the real one - inflated, in the flattering direction, and invisible because 3,000 out-of-fold predictions reads as a large sample rather than a repeated small one. On imbalanced financial labels a model that learned nothing predicts the majority every time and scores the base rate, so base_rate rides every result and beats_majority_class is a studentised stationary bootstrap rather than a comparison of two accuracies. models.champion_challenger.reasoning: pass: the row's content is the DELAY, and every decision here follows from it. In most machine learning the label arrives at prediction time; a triple-barrier label matures when a barrier is touched or the vertical one expires, which for a carry family is eight hours later. So at any instant there are THREE populations and the naive implementation collapses them: matured-and-settled, pending, and matured-but-nobody-wrote-the-outcome-down. Scoring a pending decision as a loss punishes whichever model made more recent predictions - which is ALWAYS the challenger, by construction - and dropping them silently makes the comparison shrink whenever the pipeline is behind, with nothing saying so. All three are counted and all three are reported, and the third is separated from the second because it is an operational fault rather than a result. Both models are scored on exactly the same decisions: a challenger that started shadowing on Tuesday has no opinion about Monday, and letting each be scored on whatever it has compares two different weeks and calls it a model difference. Below the floor the answer is a NoVerdict TYPE, not a SwapVerdict with should_swap=False - 'nobody has looked yet' and 'the challenger is not better' read the same to a caller and only one of them means the challenger might be. An identical challenger returns 'nothing to swap to' rather than letting the bootstrap raise on zero variance. The swap rests on validation.superior_predictive_ability rather than on a difference, because on a few hundred decisions two accuracy points is routinely noise and swapping the model that prices real positions on noise is how a system churns. The record is on disk and append-only: a comparison spans days, so held in memory it would be a session and the first restart would reset the evidence to nothing while the code kept working; a settlement is appended rather than written over its decision, because a revision is the negotiation an append-only record exists to prevent

models.stacked_ensemble.learning: pass: the meta-learner is fitted - ridge logistic regression by IRLS over the base models' out-of-fold probabilities. What is NOT fitted is the ridge strength, and that is deliberate: searching it would make the stacker's regularisation a hyperparameter fitted on the same data it is protecting. The meta-learner is deliberately the SIMPLEST thing that can combine the columns rather than another boosted tree - a tree stacker over three probability columns has enough capacity to memorise which fold a row came from, since the base models' calibration differs slightly per fold, and the whole point of stacking is that the capacity lives in the base models
models.stacked_ensemble.reasoning: pass: stacking's one famous defect is closed by the SHAPE of the API rather than by a flag. Training the meta-learner on the base models' in-sample predictions makes a stack look brilliant - on the training set a boosted tree is nearly perfect, so the stacker sees a column that is nearly the answer and learns to trust whichever base model overfit hardest - and the obvious signature, stack(base_predictions, targets), cannot prevent it: whoever calls it decides whether those predictions were out of fold, and a flag saying 'these are out-of-fold, I promise' is a comment with a colon in it. So this module takes FITTERS and calls them itself on folds it built. There is no argument through which in-sample base predictions can arrive, and both the tests and the wall probe verify the property directly by recording every call and asserting no learner was asked to predict a row it had just trained on. Four more: the folds are the project's own purged CPCV folds and the meta-learner is scored on the SAME fold structure, so the score is out of sample with respect to both levels rather than only the second - fresh random folds over the out-of-fold matrix would look better and be wrong, since those columns were produced by models that saw most of the rest of the series. Rows tested by several folds are AVERAGED, not repeated. The stack is scored against the BEST SINGLE BASE MODEL, not the base rate - a stack that beats the base rate has proved nothing, its base models already do - and base_accuracies rides the result so the comparison is auditable. A stack identical to its best base is reported as such rather than dressed up as a non-significant improvement, which for three correlated inputs is the common outcome. The sigmoid is split by sign so neither branch overflows, because exp of a large positive is inf and inf/inf is nan, which would poison a whole column silently rather than raising. The intercept is not penalised: shrinking it would pull every prediction toward 0.5 in proportion to how imbalanced the labels are, a bias from the regulariser rather than from the data
models.stacked_ensemble.depth: pass: the leak-check is a behaviour and it is exercised on every board pass rather than asserted - the probe records the module's own calls and goes FAILING if any base learner is asked to predict a row it trained on, and separately runs a REDUNDANT pair and fails if the module reports it as worth combining, because a stacker that always finds an improvement is reporting the fit rather than the finding. `converged` is reported rather than assumed: coefficients from an unfinished solve are wherever the last step left them, and two stacks are not comparable when one did not finish. It is another consumer of validation.trial_registry and of the purged CPCV folds, and registers the whole stack as ONE trial - it answers one question. The honest boundary: the probe stacks SYNTHETIC base models and says so, because no two real models exist to stack yet

Every other model in this package is fitted on market data, of which there is a lot; this one is fitted on the EXPERIMENT LEDGER, of which there are a few dozen rows and will be a few hundred for a long time. A meta-model over thirty trials is a lookup table with a p-value it has not earned, and the fact that it produces coefficients is not evidence it learned anything. FitRefused is a returned VALUE rather than an exception, because 'not yet' is the expected state for months and a board should render it without a try block. Two biases are named and one of them is measured: SELECTION - the ledger holds what somebody chose to try, so a model over it learns the searcher's habits at least as much as the market's, and largest_family_share is reported precisely because it does NOT improve with N, only with a broader search; and ABANDONMENT - a trial that raised has no outcome, so conditioning on completed trials conditions on completion, which cannot be closed structurally the way features.cross_sectional closes survivorship and is therefore made visible instead. The split is CHRONOLOGICAL, because random K-fold over the ledger would train on trials run after the ones it tests and the whole question is whether past experiments predict future ones; pinned by a test that plants the relationship only in the later half and asserts the fit scores zero. One-hot levels are taken from the TRAINING half only, so a family appearing only after the split creates no column - a lookahead through the schema rather than through the values. Goal-doc 5a.5 calls per-symbol tuning 'the single most dangerous thing that could be implemented here' - one setup on 1,290 symbols is one hypothesis with 1,290 samples, and 1,290 hypotheses the moment a parameter is fitted per instrument. So there is exactly ONE expression, evaluated identically on every candidate, and the only per-symbol quantity is the funding percentile, which is a rank against that symbol's own visible history from features.funding_basis. What IS learned, in the sense 5a.5 asks for, is the ACCEPTANCE THRESHOLD: it is the capacity-th best net carry among everything that cleared the cost gate, so it rises with opportunity flow rather than being a number somebody chose. `capacity` is a portfolio constraint, not a fitted value, and it lands in the Trial Registry with every run. A test checks that no module-level mapping is keyed by symbol
strategy.funding_carry.reasoning: pass: three defects found by RUNNING it, each of which flatters. (1) The universe was an optional argument defaulting to None, which skipped the filter - and the filter is what establishes that a hedge leg exists at all. Unfiltered, the top four proposals were BTWUSDT, ESPORTSUSDT, SPORTFUNUSDT and STARUSDT at 79-137% annualised, and 173 candidates had no spot market to hedge against: the funding was paying for exactly the risk the hedge was supposed to remove. It is now a REQUIRED argument and a missing venue raises UniverseNotSupplied. This is the defect that cannot be seen in the output - the proposals look excellent. (2) A vocabulary collision made every spot quote refuse, silently and totally: the STORE's venue is a FEED (`binance-spot`) and the FEE table's is an EXCHANGE (`('binance','spot')`), so 868 of 868 binance perps declined cost_refused. Neither table was wrong - they disagree about what a word means - and HEDGE_VENUES now declares both halves. (3) The capacity rule over-fills on ties: the threshold landed on 1071 bps and 58 symbols cleared it because 48 sit at binance's 1 bp DEFAULT funding rate. Ties are reported through over_capacity rather than broken, because choosing between identical opportunities would invent a preference in a module whose contract is that it proposes and the arbiter selects - and the overflow is itself the finding, since a screen whose acceptance threshold lands on the venue's default rate is ranking noise, not carry. Beyond those: the cost gate prices BOTH legs, since a delta-hedged carry pays two round trips and pricing one is a factor-of-two error in the flattering direction; the carry number is labelled a FORECAST because the expectation inside it is 'the next settlement's rate equals the last one', and funding is persistent enough that it is usually nearly right, which is the property that stops anyone checking; the hedge is matched on EXACT ticker equality across a declared venue pair rather than by stripping a suffix, and the residual risk is stated; and the default action is stand aside, with `declined` counting by stage so an empty list from a quiet market is distinguishable from one from a broken feed FOURTH, and the worst of them, found after the row was already committed: the cost gate compared the ANNUALISED carry against the ONE-OFF round-trip cost - 1095 bps against 24 bps, PASS - but an annual rate is only earned by holding for a year. Over one 8-hour settlement that trade earns 1 bp and pays 24, a 23 bp loss, and needs 24 settlements to break even. The gate passed trades that lose money on every realistic holding period and the output looked outstanding. It now gates on carry EARNED over a declared holding_settlements, restoring the spec's own rule that 'expected carry per settlement must exceed quote_round_trip_cost for the round trip'; the annualised figure is kept in a separate field because it is what compares two instruments with different schedules, and separate fields are what stop the two being confused again.
